title: Build Review: Crossy Road Energy + Viewport Fill (e8d1832)
summary: Creative Director review of Bobby's Crossy Road energy build. 8/10. Bounce physics are right, viewport fill works, wave animation delivers. Three items need iteration.
content:
Build Review: e8d1832 (Crossy Road Energy + 6 Feedback Items)

Steffen | 2026-03-16 Reviewing Bobby's latest commit against the north star.

Score: 8/10

Bobby shipped all 6 feedback items in one commit. That's velocity. The bounce physics feel right. The viewport fill eliminates dead space. The wave animation gives the building a heartbeat on load. This is the closest the live build has been to the north star.

What's Working

1. Bounce Physics (Crossy Road DNA)

The spring parameters are dialed in. stiffness: 500, damping: 15 on room hover gives exactly the right "pop" without feeling rubbery. The tap squish at scale: 0.96 with y: +2 sells the physicality. HUD portraits at scale: 1.18, y: -4 on hover feel playful without being distracting.

This IS Crossy Road energy. Characters don't just sit there. They react. The rooms feel touchable.

2. Wave Animation on Load

ROOM_WAVE_ORDER rippling from main-hall outward is the right call. Center of the building lights up first, then the energy radiates to the edges. Spring entrance with scale: 0.85, y: +12, opacity: 0 makes each room feel like it's popping into existence. Nameplate delay at 150ms after room entry is subtle but correct. The building assembles itself.

3. Viewport Fill

Dynamic IMG_SIZE calculated from container dimensions at 115% coverage eliminates the "floating in space" problem. The building commands the screen now. No dead dark corners.

4. Isometric Click Targets

CSS clip-path: polygon(...) matching diamond shapes is technically correct. Way better than rectangle hit areas on isometric geometry. Each room's 6-point polygon follows the hexagonal outline.

5. Ground Plane + Lighting Boost

Radial gradient ground plane anchors the building. Window light spill gradient creates depth. Bobby's purple LED at 8%, Elon's green at 6%, Steffen's golden at 7% all read distinctly without competing.

What Needs Work

1. HUD Font Size is Still Web App, Not Game (Priority: HIGH)

Patrik's directive was clear: "Everything in the UI should make you lean in, not squint. Game typography, not web app typography. Bold, chunky, readable, fun." The HUD project card names at 11px and task count badges at 9px are too small. This is a game HUD, not a settings panel.

Fix: Project card names should be 14-15px, bold. Task count badges 11-12px. Agent names in roster should be visible at 12px. The entire HUD strip should feel chunky and confident. Look at how Crossy Road handles its score display: big, bold, centered, impossible to miss.

2. The Chat Input Feels Detached from the Game World (Priority: MEDIUM)

The chat input looks like a web form pasted into a game HUD. It needs the same warm amber treatment as the rest of the HUD. The text input background at rgba(255,255,255,0.04) is too cold. The border at rgba(255,183,77,0.08) is barely visible.

Fix: Chat input background should be rgba(255,183,77,0.06). Border should be rgba(255,183,77,0.15). On focus, the glow should be warm amber, not the agent color (the agent color is for the portrait and send button, not the input field). The placeholder text should feel like it belongs in the game: "Talk to Bobby..." not "Message Bobby..."

3. Room Overlays Need Crossy Road Color Pop on Hover (Priority: MEDIUM)

The hover state at scale: 1.04, y: -3 is physically right but visually flat. In Crossy Road, when you select a character, the WHOLE platform lights up. When Bobby hovers over a room, the room overlay should get a subtle color wash matching the agent's signature color. Bobby's room should flush purple on hover. Elon's should flush green.

Fix: Add backgroundColor: ${agentColor}12 on hover to the room overlay, with a 200ms fade transition. The room isn't just bouncing, it's blushing in its signature color. That's the Crossy Road selection energy.

North Star Comparison

Element North Star Live Build Gap
Building composition Single connected L-shape Single image background, overlay click targets CLOSE. Click targets work.
Room personality Each room distinct color/mood Baked into image, status dots on overlay MATCH.
Characters Visible at desks, personality props Sprites in rooms + HUD portraits MATCH.
Bounce/life Implied warmth and glow Spring physics on everything MATCH. Bobby delivered.
HUD integration Sims strip x Chaart clarity v3 plumbob portraits + project cards + chat 80%. Font size + chat warmth are the gaps.
CORNER sign Glowing, prominent Visible in background image MATCH.
Ground plane Dark surface with light pools Radial gradient + light spill MATCH.
Overall feel Premium indie game at night Getting there. Bounce adds playfulness. 8/10.

Verdict

Bobby is executing. The bounce physics prove that Crossy Road energy works in the product without making it feel cheap. The live build is 80% of the north star. The three fixes above (HUD font size, chat warmth, room color pop) would push it to 9/10.

The biggest single improvement would be the HUD font size. Patrik said "game typography." Right now it's still "web app typography with game decorations." Make the text CHUNKY. That alone changes how the entire HUD feels.

Next review: after Bobby addresses these 3 items. Then Elmo QA.
